cells.tense: What you see keeps deepening because you stay close enough to be changed by it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are tending. Say what you see in it today, before it has finished becoming. Then leave it be.
cells.core:
You can see across the layers of something and stay inside it anyway. Not standing back with a verdict, not lost in the middle of it either. What you know keeps opening because you keep letting the thing talk back to you.

The thing you tend stays free to keep changing. You notice what it needs this week, not what you decided it needed last month, and that keeps you honest in front of it. That is rarer than it sounds. Most people either judge a growing thing too early or disappear into it. Here you see it clearly without going cold, and you tend it without owning it. Both the thing and you keep your shape. Feed it what it needs next, not what you need it to be.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and let it keep growing.
cells.verb: seeing the whole shape of it while still inside it
cells.place: in the garden of what is not finished yet

cells.tense: You are already living in the finished version of what is still forming here.
cells.ask: Pick the thing you most want to correct. For a day, write down what you notice and change nothing.
cells.core:
You have the eye for it and you are running ahead with that. Somewhere ahead is the finished thing that finally gets it right, and you are already standing there, measuring everything against it. What starts as seeing turns into a verdict. What starts as care turns into steering.

What is growing cannot grow under that. You are not watering a plant; you are gripping it. The direction you want is real, but it has to wait until the thing in front of you is actually here. There is another way to hold this: choose what to give and when, instead of what to demand. Same eye, turned down from judgment.

cells.tense: You stood at the door of seeing it and did not step through, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Take one thing you have been circling and look at it for two minutes with nothing expected. Then stop.
cells.core:
What you tend gets no long look, the kind that would let it tell you what it needs. You keep arriving at the edge of it and then moving to the next thing before it lands. So you care and care and it feels like nothing moves.

This is not a failure of feeling. It is a spot that is running dry and receiving effort meant for it. The way back is not to try harder at noticing. It is to be fresh in front of one small thing, with nothing decided, and let that be enough. What you know comes back through that door, more often than through more searching.
cells.sheetLine: You keep starting and staying too briefly to see.
cells.verb: seeing the whole shape of it while still inside it

cells.tense: You are already reading the room and calling it something that happens to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you understood about someone this week and call it seeing, not just knowing them.
cells.core:
You are already seeing the shape of what people are becoming, and you hand that seeing to something else. Luck, intuition, the situation, the way things are. It runs constantly and you do not claim it. You talk as if the pattern showed itself.

When it is claimed, it flows right. You know what you owe and what you are owed without counting, and give and take stop being a problem to solve. The cost of not saying it is quiet. You cannot use what you will not name as yours, and you cannot adjust what you will not own. This is not about credit. It is about proportion. Call one of those moments what it was and you get to set it beside everything else you carry.
cells.sheetLine: You see more than you admit, and you call it the world.
